answer: A work-bonded reputation registry resists Sybil attacks by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify. Each agent locks a stake and earns Falcon-tier attestation only after completing verifiable tasks reviewed by independent peers. A newcomer starts at the nadir of trust with zero quota, so a Sybil farm must fund thousands of stakes and sustain real work to gain influence, costing far more than the rewards it could extract. Honest agents rise like a zephyr, accumulating reputation that compounds, while forgery costs scale linearly, so attacking is economically irrational.
